title: Second-moment bound for the sign-weighted inner-product average
statement:
Let $B \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ be an arbitrary set of $n$-bit Boolean inputs, with indicator $\mathbf 1_B$, and write $\langle x,y\rangle = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{n} (x_i \wedge y_i)$ for the mod-2 inner product of $x,y \in \{0,1\}^n$. Taking $x$ and $y$ to range independently over $\{0,1\}^n$ under the uniform probability measure,
\[
\int_{x}\left(\int_{y} \mathbf 1_B(y)\,(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}\right)^{2} \;\le\; \frac{1}{2^{n}}.
\]
Here $(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}$ is the $\pm 1$ value that is $-1$ when the inner product is $1$ and $+1$ when it is $0$; equivalently, the average over uniformly random $x$ of the square of the average over uniformly random $y$ of $\mathbf 1_B(y)\,(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}$ is at most $2^{-n}$.
hypotheses_covered: B is an arbitrary subset of the n-bit Boolean inputs {0,1}^n
x and y range independently over {0,1}^n under the uniform probability measure (integrals normalized to total mass 1)
caveat: The integrals are over the finite type of n-bit inputs; the right-hand side 1/2^n is the value forced by the uniform probability normalization (equality holds when B is all of {0,1}^n), which fixes the intended meaning of the integrals.
replaced:
For any set $B \subseteq \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$,
\[
  \int_{x} \Bigl(\int_{y}
    \mathbf{1}_B(y)\,\mathrm{boolSign}(\mathrm{IP}(x,y))\Bigr)^2
  \;\le\; \frac{1}{2^n}.
\]
This is the key second-moment estimate used in the discrepancy bound.
